mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 3.0%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek yield in equities.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3.0% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces corporate profitability and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as recession fears intensify.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), the Federal Reserve typically implements accommodative policies, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100.5 for two consecutive months signals robust economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 100.5 (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1400.0 thousand units for two consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as recession risks increase.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods (HOUST < 1400.0 for 2 months).

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY) with elevated policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), aggressive monetary tightening suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and high rates (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY, FEDFUNDS > 4.0%)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the regime condition (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and declines in unemployment (UNRATE) signal a robust labor market, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate profits rise.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).
